proxies.proxy: cloud_payload.tokens_charged of the SAME opportunity in covex-v6-state-uo
proxies.actually_measures: coordinator.py:1854 writes tokens_charged = int(sub.est_tokens) and _submit_recall passes est_tokens=tokens = tokens_for_representation(rep), which is est_tokens for every representation except RECENT. So this is the session's est_tokens at uo's release instant, not at the shares arm's skip instant.
proxies.valid_for_the_claim: YES for the size question. The two arms replay the SAME trace at the same seed, est_tokens is a trace property (history_preload / history_append), and uo's release instant is within a few seconds of the shares skip. Reported with |t_uo_release - t_skip| so a reader can see the lag. Rows where uo never released are reported as est_tokens unknown and are never dropped.

proxies.proxy: the last residency.jsonl row for that session before t_skip
proxies.actually_measures: the coordinator's BELIEVED tier. residency.jsonl is written at build completion (coordinator.py:1788) and at session_end (coordinator.py:591), and the belief is promoted to gpu at exactly one place, coordinator.py:1786, inside that same completion handler. So every belief promotion is logged.
proxies.valid_for_the_claim: YES, with one hole: counts.belief_corrections_changed = 9 and belief_to_gpu = 9 at s4, the D172 telemetry corrector, which does not write a residency row. At most 9 session-events per cell could be promoted without appearing here, against 70 skips. Reported as a bound, not ignored. residency_readiness() also returns HOST-WARM when measured_tier == 'host'; no OFFLOAD_TO_HOST action is counted in any of these cells, so that branch is unreachable here.

proxies.proxy: cumulative piece_tokens of release_piece decisions for that session whose request row's t_done is before t_skip
proxies.actually_measures: built_tokens is incremented at coordinator.py:1777 inside _settle, so completion time is the right clock. Reset to 0 at session_end (cstate.py:295) and history_preload (cstate.py:315), both honoured.
proxies.valid_for_the_claim: YES; this is the quantity itself, re-derived from its own write site.

proxies.proxy: t_skip minus the first share_hold decision row carrying this opportunity id as key
proxies.actually_measures: the time from the FIRST share-admission hold of this instant to the skip. _share_ok logs one share_hold row per DISTINCT held instant (coordinator.py:1496-1509) and does NOT log the hold REASON, so this is time-held-by-the-share-gate, not time-held-by-the-oversize-rule specifically.
proxies.valid_for_the_claim: PARTIALLY. counts.share_reason_* are run totals in ITEM-PERIODS, not per instant, so the reason cannot be attributed to an instant from a committed cell. At s4 oversize_wait_for_own_type is 430 of the 1,504 + 430 + 243 + 58 + 262 denied item-periods across all three types; the share-gate hold is reported as a whole and the oversize share of it is NOT claimed. Marked unvalidated.

proxies.actually_measures: _uncached_in_flight is incremented with the PREDICTED uncached of every monitor, recall, piece and touch submission and decremented at settle; the monitor charge is B.epg_prompt_tokens(n_new) and n_new is not in any committed log, so the series cannot be replayed exactly.
proxies.valid_for_the_claim: The bound is exact and is what the classification uses: the re-check refused iff b0 + b1*u + b2*q > remaining_s, so if b0 + b1*u alone already exceeds remaining_s the SIZE PREDICTION decided it and the queue is irrelevant. That split needs no value of q.

proxies.proxy: prompt_tokens - cached_tokens on uo's request row for the same opportunity id
proxies.actually_measures: the engine's own report of what it had to prefill.
proxies.valid_for_the_claim: YES for 'would it have fitted'. It is the engine's measurement, not a prediction. It is NOT the same quantity as the policy's predicted u: u is est_tokens (a trace estimate) and prompt_tokens is the real tokenised prompt including the question, the options and the image placeholders. The two are compared as SIZES, with that difference stated.

not_recoverable_from_committed_cells.consequence: the per-skip uncached, queued_uncached_ahead, est_first_token_s, remaining_s and readiness the re-check ACTUALLY used are absent from every committed cell; every such column here is reconstructed and its proxy is declared
the per-gate-call uncached and w_by_type are likewise absent

input.verdict: all three arms carry the SAME D96 (2) fairness digest, equal to the trace's, so the three saw the same event stream; same seed, same ratio, same _L3_epg_rq30 knobs

stack.verdict: same server kind (vllm) on the same host for all three

comparison_validity.decoding: unchanged across the three arms: the recall body and its generation settings are coordinator.py's B.RECALL_GEN, which no arm overrides; the arms differ only in release policy
comparison_validity.caching: PREFIX CACHING IS ENABLED in these cells and is load-bearing for this diagnosis, not an incidental detail. The request log's `cached_tokens` and `cache_path` are the engine's own report, and on the skipped opportunities uo's cached_tokens is most of the prompt (the medians are in recall.uo_engine_uncached and in traced_unit). Every engine-side number here is therefore a WARM number and is labelled as one; no cold prefill is claimed, and nothing here is compared against a cold measurement.

readiness_sensitivity.verdict: the classification does not depend on the residency reconstruction: the maximally generous readiness gives the same class-(a) count

reconstruction_control.what: every robot recall the shares arm RELEASED must satisfy b0 + b1*u <= remaining_s under the reconstructed u, because the re-check let it through
reconstruction_control.note: a violation means the reconstructed u is too large and the skip table must not be read; tokens_charged is read from the SHARES cell's own outcomes row here, not from uo, so this control does not depend on the cross-arm proxy
reconstruction_control.how_to_read_a_violation: a single violation at s7 (opp0003027) is the residency hole named above: the row is reconstructed COLD, and at GPU-WARM its u would be est 16,681 less built 1,024 = 15,657, giving 2.9240 s against 2.9294 s of slack, which is feasible by 5 ms. So the violation is one belief correction that residency.jsonl does not carry, it is in the direction that OVERSTATES u, and `readiness_sensitivity` shows the classification is unchanged when every skip is given the generous readiness instead.

on_time_set_reconciliation.note: net_loss must equal check2.loss_questions; the split says how much of the loss is skips and how much is lateness

traced_unit.register: ONE traced unit, the median class-a skip by predicted/engine ratio
traced_unit.which_budget_bound_the_decision: the RELEASE RE-CHECK, on the size term: the skip is logged by release_recheck.LOG_KIND at coordinator.py:1255, which returns at 1263 BEFORE the share gate at 1269 and before the accelerator budget at 1273, so neither the share allocator nor the budget spent anything on this opportunity
